questions.def: "Enough" means the amount needed is available.
questions.question: She has ___ money to buy a new car.

questions.def: "Enough" indicates a sufficient quantity.
questions.question: There aren't ___ chairs for everyone.

questions.def: Use "many" with countable nouns like friends.
questions.question: He has much friends in this city now.

questions.def: "Have" is correct after 'don't' to express lack of time.
questions.question: I don't ___ time to go shopping today.

questions.def: "Some" is used for an unspecified amount.
questions.question: We need ___ sugar for the cake.

questions.def: "Any" is used in questions.
questions.question: Do you have ___ questions?

questions.def: Use "much" with uncountable nouns like cake.
questions.question: She ate many of the cake that was left.

questions.def: "Eat" is the base form after "didn't".
questions.question: He didn't ___ any bread.

questions.def: "A little" is used with uncountable nouns for small amounts.
questions.question: There is ___ milk in the fridge.

questions.def: "Few" means almost none (negative meaning).
questions.question: I have ___ friends. I am lonely.

questions.def: "Little" means almost no money.
questions.question: I have little money to buy a new house.

questions.def: "Read" (past participle) is used after "haven't".
questions.question: I haven't ___ many books this year.

questions.def: "Little" is used for uncountable nouns like time.
questions.question: She has ___ time to relax.

questions.def: "A few" is used for countable nouns (positive meaning).
questions.question: There are only ___ apples left.

questions.def: "Much" is correct because experience is uncountable.
questions.question: He has much experience in this field already.

questions.def: "Worked" (past participle) is used after "has".
questions.question: He has ___ many hours this week.

questions.def: "Some" is used to indicate an unspecified amount.
questions.question: I have ___ information for you.

questions.def: "Any" is used in questions for uncountable nouns.
questions.question: Did you buy ___ milk?

questions.def: Use "many" with countable nouns like people.
questions.question: There are much people at the party tonight.

questions.def: "Drunk" (past participle) is used after "haven't".
questions.question: I haven't ___ much water today.

questions.def: "Much" is used with uncountable nouns.
questions.question: There isn't ___ coffee left.

questions.def: "Many" is used with countable nouns.
questions.question: I have ___ problems.

questions.def: 'A few' is correct with countable nouns.
questions.question: He has a little friends in his class today.

questions.def: "Gone" (past participle) is used after "have".
questions.question: Have you ___ to Italy?

questions.def: "Some" is used for an unspecified amount of help.
questions.question: She needs ___ help with her homework.

questions.def: "Any" is used in negative sentences.
questions.question: He doesn't have ___ brothers or sisters.

questions.def: Use "little" with uncountable nouns like time.
questions.question: She has few time to finish the project.

questions.def: "Seen" (past participle) is used after "haven't".
questions.question: I haven't ___ him in years.

questions.def: "Many" is used with countable nouns.
questions.question: There are ___ people waiting outside.

questions.def: "Any" is used in questions.
questions.question: Do you have ___ sugar for tea?
